apply_contract.primary_form: single-line shell command joined with && and backslashes; copy-paste as one input from TTY
apply_contract.awk_pattern_rationale: Closed-form (with `happy-restart\.sh` segment) is preferred over the open-prefix form recommended at proposal markdown line 31 because Grep confirmed there are exactly two `^=== (BEGIN|END)` lines in the markdown — both forms would work — but closed-form is strictly safer (fails loudly if marker drifts). Open-prefix form would also be correct as a fallback.
apply_contract.sed_strip_rationale: Awk's range expression is inclusive on both ends, selecting lines 121..527 (407 lines). sed `1d;$d` deletes the first (BEGIN marker) and last ($d = last line, the END marker), leaving lines 122..526 = 405 script lines.
apply_contract.crlf_defense: tr -d '\r' before awk, defending against accidental CRLF line endings in the markdown source.
apply_contract.atomic_write_form: stage to tempfile via mktemp; validate `wc -l >= 400` AND `head -1` is `#!/bin/bash` AND `tail -1` matches the proposal's last line; then `mv` atomically; finally `chmod +x`.
apply_contract.exact_command_string: TMP=$(mktemp /tmp/happy-restart-stage.XXXXXX) && cat /dev/shm/dev-workspace/happy-dev/docs/dev/proposal-c1-happy-restart-refactor-20260504-223115.sh.md | tr -d '\r' | awk '/^=== BEGIN happy-restart\.sh ===$/,/^=== END happy-restart\.sh ===$/' | sed '1d;$d' > "$TMP" && LINES=$(wc -l < "$TMP") && echo "staged_lines=$LINES" && [ "$LINES" -ge 400 ] && head -1 "$TMP" | grep -q '^#!/bin/bash$' && tail -1 "$TMP" | grep -q '^log "Services:\$SUMMARY_PARTS"$' && mv "$TMP" /root/bin/happy-restart.sh && chmod +x /root/bin/happy-restart.sh && echo APPLY_OK

codex_consult.feedback_summary: Codex skill invocation blocked by `pretool-bash-safety.sh` because the prompt contained the substring `happy-restart`. The hook (per concern C3) blocks ANY subagent bash command containing this substring — including codex CLI invocation. Per Subagent Hook Discipline rule 1, BA paused, did NOT circumvent the hook (no /tmp wrapper, no substring obfuscation), and per BA codex graceful-fallback protocol substituted self-review covering all six adversarial questions (a..f).
codex_consult.feedback_incorporated: Self-review substituted. Self-review answers: (a) closed-form awk pattern `/^=== BEGIN happy-restart\.sh ===$/,/^=== END happy-restart\.sh ===$/` is correct given the verified markers at lines 121 and 527 — selects 407 inclusive lines. (b) `sed '1d;$d'` correctly strips first (BEGIN) and last (END) lines of awk's output, leaving 405 script lines. (c) Open-prefix form would also work given Grep confirmed only 2 hits, but closed-form is strictly safer (fails loud on marker drift) — adopted closed-form. (d) Residual modes mitigated: (i) CRLF — added `tr -d '\r'` defense; (ii) shell line-wrap — single-line form joined with && and \\ adopted; (iii) symlink — `mv` semantics work in both regular-file and symlink target cases; (iv) disk-full mid-write — adopted atomic-mv from tempfile staging plus `wc -l >= 400` and head/tail content gates so destination is never touched on extraction failure. (e) Verification ordering revised: `wc -l` precedes `bash -n` (line-count fails first if extraction is broken); added `head -3` and `tail -1` content spot-checks; no-arg real run kept as V4 (it IS the AC4 regression-guard), placed after V3 fail-closed test to verify dispatch table works for unknowns first. (f) Pre-apply .bak provides primary recovery; the existing `.bak.20260505-095913` provides secondary baseline; atomic-mv-from-tempfile eliminates the only failure mode the .bak alone could not cover (destination corruption mid-write). The three-tier defense (atomic-mv + .bak.preapply + .bak.baseline) is complete.
